question.text: Ms. Kavitha Raman's Cat I AIF-VCF invests in pre-Series-A SaaS startups. Her portfolio company Aether Tech is 4 years old with INR 30 crore in turnover, working on an AI-driven supply-chain product. Per the DPIIT definition of 'startup' referenced in NISM Ch 2.3.1, does Aether Tech still qualify as a startup?

answer.text: No — DPIIT classifies a company as startup only if it is less than 3 years old.
Yes — DPIIT defines a startup as a company not more than 10 years old with turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any financial year, and engaged in innovation/scalability.
No — turnover above INR 25 crore disqualifies a company from being a startup per DPIIT.
Yes, but only if it is registered as a Private Limited Company under the Companies Act 2013 and generates no revenue.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.3.1, DPIIT defines a startup as a business not more than 10 years old with turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any financial year, engaged in innovation, development, improvement of products, or a scalable business model with high employment/wealth potential. Aether Tech at 4 years and INR 30 crore comfortably meets both limbs. The Trap: Option A uses an older shorter age cap that does not match the DPIIT definition in the workbook. Option C mis-states the turnover ceiling at INR 25 crore — the source states INR 100 crore. Option D adds a zero-revenue and Private Limited registration requirement that does not exist in the source. Note: Apply the DPIIT criteria directly — age not more than 10 years, turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any financial year, and an innovation/scalability orientation.
